_comment: Hand-written normalization for the Little Monkey Toes catalog.
Every entry below was decided by reading the actual size run, vendor and
product it appears on. Nothing here is inferred by pattern matching,
because pattern matching is exactly what breaks on this catalog: '2Y'
means a youth shoe size on Footmates and a duplicate of '2T' on Properly
Tied, and no rule can tell those apart from the string alone.
That is also why sizes are split into a global map and a per-vendor map.
The global map holds only labels that mean the same thing everywhere in
this catalog -- case, punctuation and fraction-vs-decimal. Anything whose
meaning depends on who made the garment lives under by_vendor.

_note: Applied to Shopify product option values and to the matching variant
selectedOptions. Where a rename collides with a value the product
already carries, the two variants are the same physical size listed
twice and get merged -- see merge_policy.
A semantic merge is normally refused when the duplicate holds stock,
because choosing one side deletes sellable units and summing risks
overselling. These are the cases where the brand's published chart
settles it and the owner has accepted a stock recount afterwards.
Stock is summed rather than discarded -- 6Y's 4 units join 6's 8 --
so nothing is written off before the recount happens.

Properly Tied.6Y: Properly Tied publish no Y sizes; the run is 5, 6, 7 then YS (8).
Properly Tied.YS: 'YS' and 'YS (8)' are the same published size.

global._case_only: Lowercase toddler and 6X sizes; Shopify treats '2t' and '2T' as different filter values, which splits every Shop-by-size chip in two.
global._word_order: L'Amour writes its baby shoe sizes the other way round from Footmates and Salt Water.
global._newborn: Widgeon spells out Newborn; the rest of the catalog uses NB.
global._trailing_zero: Footmates ships some shoe runs as '3.0' and others as '3'.
global._fractions: Half shoe sizes appear as both '3 1/2' and '3.5' across Footmates and Petit Jolie. Decimals sort correctly in a filter; fractions do not.
global._combined: J Bailey lists its 4T as '4T/4R'; the rest of that run is plain.
global._jefferies_case: Jefferies capitalises 'Shoe Size' on three of six sock sizes and 'Shoe size' on the other three.

_note: Properly Tied's published run is exactly:
confirmed against the brand's own chart as reproduced by two
stockists (Cottontails Monroe, Tiny Town). The brand's spelling is
the target, which is why the annotations use a slash rather than
the hyphen the source data happened to use.
Two problems, both inside this one vendor.
First, youth sizes are written both bare and annotated -- 'YS' on 20
products and 'YS (8)' on 45. Same size.
Second, 'Mallard Shorts' and one other product carry a duplicate
encoding of the whole run: 2Y/3Y/4Y alongside 2t/3t/4t and 5Y/6Y/7Y
alongside 5/6/7, with a separate variant for each. There is no Y
size anywhere in the published chart, so these are the same garment
listed twice.
Chus is sized in EU. One product spells out the US equivalent and
the other does not, so the same shoe size appears as both '21' and
The US values below are the brand's own published chart, not the
store's annotations and not a calculated conversion. The two
disagree in three places, and the brand wins: EU 23 is US 6.5-7 (the
store said 7), EU 30 is US 12-12.5 (the store said 12.5), and EU 32
is Y1 (the store said '1 youth'). Chus also runs small enough that
they publish half-size spans deliberately, so flattening 6.5-7 to a
single number would be discarding fitting advice, not tidying it.

left_alone._note: Recorded so a later pass does not mistake these for oversights.
left_alone.1Y / 2Y / 3Y / 4Y / 5Y / 6Y / 7Y on Foot: Genuine youth shoe sizes -- the run goes 11, 12, 13, then 1Y. Renaming these the way Properly Tied's are renamed would move a size-1 youth shoe into the toddler bucket.
left_alone.1 YR / 2 YR / 4 YR / 6 YR (Bob & Blossom: Age-in-years sizing, internally consistent and used by no other vendor. Mapping it onto '2T' would assert a fit equivalence the vendor never published.
left_alone.7/8, 8/10, 10/12 (Prodoh) and 2/3, 5/6,: Real spanning sizes, not two sizes joined by a slash.
left_alone.C4-C13, J1-J4 (Floafers): Child and Junior, the brand's own scheme, already consistent.
left_alone.XS (3/4) / S (6/8) / M (8/10) (Mustard &: Two vendors' letter runs that disagree about what a Small is, and both are correct: Prodoh's chart publishes XS as 7/8 and Mustard & Ketchup's publishes XS as 3/4. The brand's chart is the source of truth, so a Small meaning a 4-year-old at one label and an 8-year-old at another is left standing. Parents in this category read the parenthetical, which is why both runs keep it.
left_alone.Infant / Toddler (Apple of My Isla bib): Descriptive, and a bib has no numeric size.
left_alone.Large (Chus): Chus publish EU sizes only -- there is no Large anywhere in their chart -- so this is a data-entry error rather than a size. It is exactly one variant, 'Light Blue / Large' on CHRIS Canvas T-Straps (SKU-265-Large-...), holding 10 units. Chus has since been dropped from the live storefront, so there is nothing left to cross-check it against, and picking an EU size for it would be inventing inventory. Left for the BigCommerce admin export to settle.
left_alone.Numeric sizes shared between shoes and c: A '7' is both a shirt size and a shoe size in this catalog. That is not fixable by renaming -- it needs the size filter scoped by product category, which the taxonomy assignments below make possible.

_note: 74 types for 351 products, with singular/plural pairs splitting several
in half. Footwear takes the plural form Shopify's own taxonomy uses;
garments take the singular unless the word is only ever plural.

_left_alone.One-Piece vs One-Piece Swimsuit: One product each, and 'One-Piece' could be a bodysuit rather than swimwear. Needs a look at the garment, not a rule.
_left_alone.Lounge Set vs Loungewear: One is a two-piece set, the other a category. Not the same thing.
_left_alone.Shoes / Lace Up Shoe / Saddle Shoe / Ten: Four genuinely different footwear styles; only 'Shoes' is vague and it is a single product.

tags._note: Only the four pairs that differ purely by separator. Hyphenated wins because it is the more used form in every pair.

_left_alone.vendor-name tags: 'pleat', 'prodoh', 'j bailey' and similar duplicate the vendor field. Harmless, and they may be driving existing automated collections, so removing them is a merchandising decision rather than a cleanup.

_note: Five products have no Shopify taxonomy category at all, and the bag
products that do have one disagree with each other -- backpacks split
between two categories, and a lunchbox filed under Toiletry Bags.
Category matters more here than it looks: Shopify derives the standard
product attributes that Search & Discovery groups filters around from
it, so a wrong category is a broken filter.
